summary: Lynn/Kirsch/Terhune (2023, BJPsych Advances): 'no robust neurophysiological evidence to demonstrate that hypnosis is a special or unique state.' More parsimonious to define hypnosis as procedures using verbal suggestion to modulate awareness/perception/cognition.
content: Lynn, Kirsch, Terhune et al. (2023, BJPsych Advances): 'there is no robust neurophysiological evidence to demonstrate that hypnosis is a special or unique state (Terhune 2017).' Argues 'It is more parsimonious to consider hypnosis as a set of procedures in which verbal suggestions are used to modulate awareness, perception and cognition (Terhune 2014), rather than to unnecessarily invoke special states.' Also: 54% of participants are equally or LESS suggestible following a hypnotic induction (Braffman & Kirsch 1999); no evidence of blind obedience or loss of control; spontaneous amnesia is incredibly rare.
